title: Cosmic Microwave Background
body:
The **cosmic microwave background** is radiation reaching Earth from every direction, with a
[[Blackbody Radiation|blackbody]] spectrum at 2.7 K. It is the strongest evidence for the
[[Big Bang]].

The early universe was hot enough to keep matter ionised, and free electrons scatter light, so
it was opaque. About 380,000 years in it cooled to roughly 3000 K, electrons and nuclei
combined into neutral atoms, and light was suddenly free to travel. That light has been
travelling ever since.

It was emitted at 3000 K and arrives at 2.7 K because the expansion of space stretched its
wavelength by a factor of about 1100 on the way, which is redshift applied to the whole sky.

Two features carry the information:

```
uniformity     the temperature is the same in every direction to one part in 100,000
fluctuations   the tiny departures from uniformity are the seeds of every galaxy
```

The fluctuations are the important half. They map the density variations present at 380,000
years, and gravity amplified them into the structure observed now, so the pattern is a direct
constraint on the composition of the universe and requires [[Dark Matter]] to reach
today's galaxies in the time available.

The radiation was predicted in the 1940s and found by accident in 1965 by two engineers tracing
persistent noise in a radio antenna.
